newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Ortiz says June inflation under one pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Ortiz says June inflation under one pct.

text.p: Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said on Wednesday that inflation in June will be less than one percent, which would help the country meet its goal of holding inflation to 15 percent for the year.

"In June inflation certainly once again will be less than one percent," Ortiz said in the western city of Guadalajara during a presentation of the government's three-year economic plan known as Pronafide.

In May, the consumer price index showed an increase of 0.91 percent compared to April, the smallest monthly rise in the CPI since December 1994, the same month that the peso was drastically and suddenly devalued.
"We will have the possibility of closing in on the inflationary goal of 15 percent by the end of the year," Ortiz said. "I think we will be between, say, 15 and 16 percent."
